Basilisk

Magical Beast · 2 hexes · SM +0 Basilisk [Monster Manual, page 23]

A low, heavy lizard about as long as a man is tall, running on eight short legs, rough-scaled in olive and ochre with a blunt wedge of a head. It is slow, ill-tempered and entirely unhurried, because it has no need of speed: whatever meets its glowing amber eyes stops being flesh.

Sharp TeethSharp Teeth (10): thrust 1d+1 cutting (KYOS: 2d cutting), Reach C.10thrust 1d+1 cutting (KYOS: 2d cutting)C
Petrifying GazePetrifying Gaze (10): A basilisk’s petrifying gaze spreads out in a cone 15 yards long and 15 yards wide at the end. It can select who is affected; potential victims must be looking at it. For every target, there is a Quick Contest between the basilisk’s Will (minus a range penalty taken from the Speed/Range Table) and each target’s HT. If the basilisk wins, the target is petrified. (The distinction between “paralyzed” and “petrified” generally works in their victims’ favor – e.g., they won’t starve – so the basilisk does not pay extra for this.) Someone looking at a reflection of a basilisk is not affected by its gaze. Fighting while looking in a mirror is at a -5 penalty; attacks made with closed eyes are at -10. Petrification can be removed with Remove Curse or Stone to Flesh.
